definitions.explanation: A formal Sino-Japanese prefix marking that something has already occurred or is already in place. Common in administrative, legal, and academic writing.

examples.japanese: {既|き}{婚|こん}{者|しゃ}{向|む}けのアンケートです。
examples.english: This survey is for married people.

examples.japanese: {既|き}{存|そん}のシステムを{活用|かつよう}したい。
examples.english: I want to make use of the existing system.

examples.japanese: {既|き}{発表|はっぴょう}の{論文|ろんぶん}は{審査|しんさ}{対象外|たいしょうがい}です。
examples.english: Already-published papers are excluded from review.

notes:
Bound prefix, never used standalone. Marks a state as already established or completed.

COMPOUNDS:
- {既|き}{婚|こん}: married (already wed)
- {既|き}{存|そん}: existing; pre-existing
- {既|き}{成|せい}: ready-made; established
- {既|き}{知|ち}: known; already-known
- {既|き}{往|おう}{歴|れき}: medical history (literally 'already-past history')

SIMILAR PREFIXES:
- {未|み}〜: not yet; un- — the direct antonym ({未|み}{婚|こん} unmarried, {未|み}{知|ち} unknown)
- {旧|きゅう}〜: former; old- — focuses on what something used to be, not on completion
